status.title: Finders Keepers
status.build: finders_keepers_sprites.nex (as published in nxc: figures as sprites over the XOR plotter, the painter skipped for them)
status.software: replay IDENTICAL on 4 recordings (52,127 frames); unit cases incl. four CPU speeds; 9 negatives detected
status.hardware: Tang board: loads with automap on and leftover sprites, plays

techniques.target: readers of the screen and attributes: the plotter's own XOR, LDIR fills, the painter; no logic reads figure pixels or colours
the XOR plotter 0x9A05 kept; figure n = sprite n over its own pixels in its ink, the painter skipped for it
Sinclair 48K ROM as alt ROM image 1, hooks at 0x386E
28 MHz inside each hook, the caller's NR 7 kept on the stack and put back

results.scope: 4 machine-played recordings (52,127 frames, rooms 0-22 entered); unit cases for the plot, room and erase-all hooks at four CPU speeds; 9 negatives; no human recording; no hardware timing

pacing.coverage: Hook cost counted in the simulator over the four recordings; Tang board and OverSpec play; no JNext timing against the original.
pacing.result: The plot hook runs at 28 MHz and the painter is skipped for sprite figures, so a frame does no more work at 3.5 MHz than the original; not measured on JNext.

dependencies.coverage: Every screen and attribute reader in the four recordings (scan); the plotter, the painter, room set-up (8 callers) and the erase-all before a window.
dependencies.result: The game never reads figure pixels or colours back: the XOR stays on the ULA, the painter is skipped for figures that become sprites.

feasibility.decision: Every figure with its own ink as sprite n over its own pixels in its ink, the painter skipped for it; whole-cell figures kept as drawn (the defaults).
feasibility.next_experiment: A human recording through the castle rooms: replay IDENTICAL with every negative control caught.
